sections.h2: Where is the Lebanon County Recorder of Deeds, and when is it open?
sections.html:
Lebanon County keeps its land records in Room 107 of the Municipal Building at 400 South 8th Street in the city of Lebanon, PA 17042. The office answers questions at 717-228-4447 and is staffed Monday through Friday, opening at 8:30 in the morning and closing at 4:30 in the afternoon

Everything that touches title to land in the county gets filed here: deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, easements, plans, and also UCC financing filings and notary bonds. A seller meets this office twice. The deed from the old owner to you was recorded here when you bought, and the deed you sign at closing goes onto the same record. If a mortgage is being paid off from your sale proceeds, the lender's satisfaction piece also lands on the county record, usually a few weeks after the payoff.

The staff will help you find a record, but they will not tell you how to word a deed or whether a name should come off one. Their own FAQ says the office is a custodian of records and sends those questions to an attorney.

sections.h2: What fees come with filing a Lebanon County deed?
sections.html:
A standard deed or mortgage costs $91.75 to record under the fee schedule that took effect November 12, 2025. That base price covers up to four pages and four names, and it already contains the affordable housing fee, the records improvement fee, the parcel identifier fee and the court and access-to-justice surcharges, so those do not show up as separate line items.

A few smaller charges can matter on a sale:

  • A Statement of Value that has attachments adds $2.00 for each attachment page. The duplicate copy for the state carries no charge.
  • Sending a document by email to the office costs $5.00 plus $0.50 for each page.
  • A returned check costs $30.00.
  • Copies run $0.50 per page on sheets up to tabloid size, and oversized pages add $5.00.

The office takes cash or checks only. Write the check to the Recorder of Deeds for the exact amount, because fees and transfer taxes must be paid when the document is presented.

sections.h2: What does a Lebanon County deed need before the office will record it?
sections.html:
The deed must show a Uniform Parcel Identifier, called a UPI, on page one, and that number must be certified by the county Assessment Office. The certification happens electronically inside the courthouse. If you do not have the number, call Assessment at 717-228-4425 or use the county property viewer to look the parcel up by address.

The county's recording instructions add several other requirements:

  • A signed certificate of residence for the grantee on every deed, and for the mortgagee on every mortgage or assignment.
  • Type no smaller than 10 point, and a legal acknowledgment before a notary.
  • A typed English translation attached to any document written in another language.
  • Page numbers or numbering that shows the filing order when several documents belong to one transaction.
  • Where a parcel straddles two or more municipalities or school districts, the percentage lying in each, so the local levy can be split.
  • A return envelope, addressed and stamped, big enough to carry the originals home.

A Statement of Value, the state's REV-183 form, is filed in duplicate with its attachments. It is required when the deed does not state the full price, when the transfer is a gift or has no consideration, when an exemption is claimed, and when the property was sold at a tax claim or sheriff sale. The county notes that a statement is not needed when full consideration is paid, when the transfer is between close family members, or when the grant is an easement to a public utility. Fill in every block, sign it, and date it with the settlement or acceptance date.

sections.h2: How much realty transfer tax is due on a Lebanon County sale?
sections.html:
The state's realty transfer tax is 1 percent of a property's value, paid at the counter with the filing fee. Per the state revenue department, grantor and grantee answer for it jointly. A local levy rides on top, divided between the school district and municipality that cover the house. Call the office or your settlement agent to learn the combined percentage for your street address.

Exemptions cover some family transfers, inheritance by will or intestacy, and government transfers. Anyone claiming one is pointed to the state rules, and the REV-183 must lay out the basis. The county FAQ also gives Lebanon County's assessed ratio, known as the common level ratio, as 1.39 percent that also appears on the Statement of Value.

In a typical sale the settlement agent works out the tax and delivers a check. The purchase agreement says which side absorbs the cost.

sections.h2: How long does recording take, and can I record electronically?
sections.html:
According to the county, most filings are back with their owners the next business day, by pickup, mail or electronic return. Each document is received, reviewed and keyed in, sent to Assessment to certify the UPI, returned for recording, and then proofread. Documents are recorded in the order they arrive, so a heavy day can lengthen the wait.

Electronic recording is accepted through Simplifile, CSC and ePN, three vendors the office lists by name, and confirmation can come back in minutes. A mailed filing needs a check for the exact amount plus the return envelope.

Landex, the county's records vendor, also runs record alerts tied to a parcel number. Owners of a rental house or of a home left empty after an inheritance may want to ask the Recorder of Deeds how to sign up.

sections.h2: How do I look up deeds and mortgages recorded in Lebanon County?
sections.html:
Lebanon County was established in 1813, and its recorded documents from 1925 to the present can be searched online through Landex. Anything older has to be viewed at the office in Room 107. Anyone may view the records, with one exception: military discharge papers (DD214 forms) are kept private. Veterans can record a DD214 for free and may get a Veterans ID Card.

Phone help is limited, because the office is not insured for title searching. Plan to do your own search online, or hire a title company if the chain of ownership is complicated. A deed describes the land and not the buildings on it, so adding a house to a lot does not produce a new deed.

Notary commissions are handled in the same office. The notary fee is $42.00, which includes the Prothonotary fee, paid by one check payable to the Recorder of Deeds.

sections.h2: What is the Lebanon County setting like for a home sale?
sections.html:
Lebanon County covers 362 square miles in south central Pennsylvania, about 72 miles northwest of Philadelphia. It was cut from Dauphin and Lancaster counties in 1813, and the city of Lebanon serves as seat and biggest town. Census figures show 143,257 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 146,380 for 2025.

Swatara Creek drains most of the valley toward the Susquehanna, while Tulpehocken Creek near Myerstown runs east toward the Schuylkill. Interstates 78 and 81, the Pennsylvania Turnpike (I-76), and US 22, 322 and 422 all pass through. Dauphin, Lancaster, Berks and Schuylkill counties border it.

  • Larger communities by 2010 count: Lebanon, Palmyra, Cornwall, Myerstown and Cleona.
  • Colleges: Lebanon Valley College, Evangelical Seminary and the Lebanon campus of Harrisburg Area Community College.
  • Climate: a humid continental pattern, with Lebanon city averages near 29 degrees in January and 74 in July.

Whether a house sits in Lebanon city, a borough such as Palmyra, or a township changes which municipality and school district receive the local transfer tax, so confirm your municipality before you estimate closing costs.

faqs.q: What is the base deed fee in Lebanon County?
faqs.a: Under the schedule effective November 12, 2025, the base fee is $91.75 and includes up to four names over four pages. Each extra page costs $4.00 and each extra name $1.00. The county accepts cash or check only.

faqs.q: Does Lebanon County require a parcel number on a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The Uniform Parcel Identifier belongs on the first page and must be certified by the Assessment Office. Call 717-228-4425 to get the number for your property.

faqs.q: Can I record a Lebanon County deed by email or mail?
faqs.a: Mail works with an exact-amount check and a stamped envelope for the return. Email submission is accepted for $5.00 plus $0.50 per page, and electronic recording through Simplifile, CSC or ePN is also available.

faqs.q: How soon will my recorded deed come back?
faqs.a: Most documents are returned the next business day. The wait depends on how many documents were filed ahead of yours, since the office records in order of arrival.

faqs.q: Who owes transfer tax on a Lebanon County sale?
faqs.a: Seller and buyer both answer to the state for it, and the tax is payable at the counter at filing. Who bears the cost in practice is set by the sales contract, so check it with your closing agent.
